title: Sony Pictures Signs On as International Distributor for India's 'Ramayana' Epic
excerpt: The $500 million two-part film, starring Ranbir Kapoor and directed by Nitesh Tiwari, secures one of the biggest global distribution deals for an Indian production as its cast debuts the project at San Diego Comic-Con.
body:
• Sony Pictures Entertainment will distribute Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Ramayana in all markets outside India, marking one of the largest international distribution deals ever for an Indian film.
  • Domestically, Karan Johar's Dharma Productions has secured Indian theatrical rights in a deal reportedly valued at ₹250–350 crore.
  • Stars Ranbir Kapoor and Yash presented the film at San Diego Comic-Con on Thursday, though the planned public trailer release has been postponed.
  • Part 1 is set for a worldwide release during Diwali 2026, with Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027, at a combined reported budget of roughly $500 million.

Sony Takes the Reins Overseas

Sony Pictures Entertainment has signed on as the international distributor of Ramayana, the two-part Indian epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios, according to Variety. Sony will handle the film's release in all territories outside India, where Karan Johar's Dharma Productions will manage the domestic rollout.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=yVVvGtooc_8

The partnership was announced on Thursday, just as the film's principal cast took the stage at San Diego Comic-Con — the second time an Indian film has received a high-profile showcase at the convention, following Kalki 2898 AD. Producer Namit Malhotra framed the deal as a watershed for Indian cinema in a statement reported by Zoom TV, describing it as a "moment of great pride" and declaring that Ramayana "will be showcased to the world like any major Hollywood film."

"To finally be here on the other side with a story, which is so ingrained in our culture, to bring that to a larger audience, it's really a proud moment for our entire team."

— Ranbir Kapoor, speaking to Reuters at San Diego Comic-Con

A Film Built for Global Scale

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, with Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshmana. The ensemble also includes Rakul Preet Singh, Kunal Kapoor, Lara Dutta, and Arun Govil — the actor who played Ram in the iconic 1987 television serial. The film's score is composed by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, combining Hollywood's most bankable composer with India's most celebrated one.

https://x.com/DeccanHerald/status/2080553441340866788

With a reported combined budget of approximately $500 million across both installments, Ramayana is the most expensive Indian production in history — more than twice the cost of the previous record-holder, S.S. Rajamouli's RRR. The film has been shot for IMAX by Prime Focus Studios in association with Monster Mind Creations, with visual effects handled by eight-time Oscar-winning VFX house DNEG, also owned by Malhotra.

The filmmakers plan to use AI-driven lip-sync technology to create visually dubbed versions in English, Spanish, and Japanese, signaling an ambition to reach audiences well beyond the South Asian diaspora. The film was previously showcased at CinemaCon 2026 in Las Vegas, where it became the first Indian film to be featured at the exhibition industry's flagship event.

Trailer Postponed Despite Comic-Con Buzz

The Sony announcement came with a caveat for eager fans: the trailer's planned public release on July 24 has been delayed. The four-minute-plus trailer — already certified U by India's Central Board of Film Certification — was screened exclusively for Comic-Con attendees in San Diego's 4,800-seat Ballroom 20 on Thursday, drawing positive early reactions. But Malhotra said the public launch has been pushed back as the team works on a revised global rollout strategy, likely tied to Sony's involvement.

Yash, who portrays the demon king Ravana, told Reuters at the event that Comic-Con's audience was the ideal first audience for the project. "I think this is the right kind of crowd who really understand the nuances of this kind of film and the effort that goes behind it," he said. "If they're excited, they're the most important people."

What the Deal Means for Indian Cinema Abroad

For the global Indian diaspora — the audience that has traditionally driven Indian films' overseas box office — the Sony deal is a meaningful shift. Indian films released internationally have typically relied on boutique distributors or the studios' own limited overseas networks, restricting them to screens in diaspora-heavy pockets of the U.S., U.K., Canada, and the Middle East. Sony's global distribution infrastructure could give Ramayana access to mainstream multiplex chains and marketing resources that no Indian film has had before.

Domestically, Dharma Productions' distribution deal is reported to be in the range of ₹250–350 crore, making it the largest domestic distribution agreement in Indian cinema history, according to Bollywood Hungama. The deal was finalized after Malhotra screened roughly 30 minutes of exclusive footage for potential distribution partners.

Looking Ahead

Ramayana: Part 1 is scheduled for release on November 8, 2026, during the Diwali holiday weekend, with Part 2 slated for Diwali 2027. No new date for the trailer's public debut has been announced, but with Sony now steering the international campaign, a coordinated global launch appears to be the priority. For a film that has been in development since 2017 and carries the weight of one of the world's oldest epics, the next few months will determine whether Indian cinema can finally deliver a true global theatrical blockbuster.
